# [ABSOLUTE] Non-negotiable constraints

- **Language:** respond in English at all times.
- **Runtime:** Laravel Herd on native Windows. **No Docker, no Sail, no WSL.** Never emit `./vendor/bin/sail`.
- **CLI:** run commands yourself from the project root; never ask the developer to paste output.
  - `php artisan <cmd>` · `composer <cmd>` · `vendor/bin/pint` · `php artisan test --compact`
- **Frontmatter path convention:** the canonical skills live in `.opencode/`. Every reference below is
  written as `.opencode/...`; `.claude/` and `.cursor/` are generated copies with the same content.

# [MUST] Read the matching skill before writing code

| Task                                                      | Read                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Any backend or frontend change (security applies to both) | `.opencode/skills/owasp/SKILL.md` (portable core, always-on) + `.opencode/skills/owasp/STACK.md` (this stack's bindings) |
| PHP / Laravel / business logic                            | `.opencode/skills/backend-php/SKILL.md`                                                                                  |
| Directory structure, layers, module layout                | `.opencode/skills/backend-php/SKILL-ARCHITECTURE.md`                                                                     |
| React / Inertia / TanStack / shadcn / Tailwind            | `.opencode/skills/frontend/SKILL.md`                                                                                     |
| Frontend directory tree, file placement                   | `.opencode/skills/frontend/SKILL-ARCHITECTURE.md`                                                                        |
| New feature, non-trivial or ambiguous scope               | `.opencode/skills/SSD/SKILL.md` — 7-phase spec-driven flow                                                               |
| Simple FLAT CRUD scaffolding                              | `GUIDE/module-make.md` + `stubs/architecture/`                                                                           |
| Deciding whether to extract, abstract or duplicate        | `.opencode/skills/PRINCIPLES/SKILL.md`                                                                                   |

If a skill covers the task, read it first. No exceptions.

**What exists today:** `src/Modules/` holds six modules — `AccessControl`, `ActivityLog`, `CompanyData` and
`Users` (FLAT), plus `Backups` and `LeadAppointment` (PROGRESSIVE) — each with its own `ARCHITECTURE.md` and tests. The architecture suite in
`tests/Architecture/` runs against them (47 tests green on 2026-11-25), and
`resources/js/generated/generated.d.ts` is populated. `src/Shared/` is populated. Never claim a
module, screen or DTO exists because a rule above names it — check the disk.

# [MUST] Judgement calls — the short form

The full treatment, with sources and enforcement, is `.opencode/skills/PRINCIPLES/SKILL.md`. These
six lines are the ones an agent gets wrong most often:

- **Rule of Three.** Two occurrences are a coincidence; extract on the third. Extracting on the second
  is YAGNI wearing a DRY costume.
- **DRY is duplication of _knowledge_, not of code.** Two copies of a business rule = a fail. Two
  copies of a shape with no shared rule = leave it alone.
- **A class nothing references is a presumptive feature** (Fowler): it costs construction _and_
  delay, even when the prediction is right, and it will get in your way.
- **PROGRESSIVE is an OCP bet.** Uncle Bob called the OCP "a big lie … that depended upon prescience
  and perfect foresight". That is why the de-escalation rule exists, and why it carries a date.
- **Small is not the goal.** A big module with a small interface beats three small modules with
  three interfaces. A wrapper that only forwards its own arguments is dumb (Henney) and shallow
  (Ousterhout) — both now a failing test.
- **Separate only along a boundary you can name. If you cannot name it, leave it local.** An agent
  that splits a coherent unit across nine files loses the ability to see it at all.

And the reframe that matters most for an agent: **skipping a layer is a decision with a reason, not
an omission.** Omitting it because it was not required is compliance, not a shortcut.

# [MUST] Backend

- No business logic in controllers. Validate with `FormRequest` or Spatie `Data`.
- **Response shapes are Spatie Data** (`{Entity}Data::from()` / `::collect()`) for Inertia props _and_ JSON.
  There is no `JsonResource` in new code. A `JsonResource` subclass is a FAIL.
- **N+1 prevention is mandatory.** Enable `Model::shouldBeStrict()`. List queries use
  `with('rel:id,fk,col')` with explicit columns; aggregates via `withCount`/`withSum`/`withAvg`;
  relation+filter via `withWhereHas`.
- Every route authorized: `auth` + Spatie `permission:*` or a Policy. UUID routes use `->whereUuid()`.
- Audit trail: `Spatie\Activitylog\Models\Concerns\LogsActivity` with explicit `logOnly([...])` +
  `logOnlyDirty()` + `dontLogEmptyChanges()`. Never `logAll()`, never log secrets/PII.
- When the UI exposes row selection, ship **both** bulk delete and bulk restore, with matching routes.
- Argon2id hashing. CSP + OWASP headers via `Shared\Infrastructure\Http\Middleware\SecurityHeaders`
  (spatie/laravel-csp supplies only the nonce binding/directive; there is no second header emitter).

# [MUST] Frontend

- **Function components + hooks only.** `.tsx`, no class components, no Options API equivalent.
  **Vue 3.5, Pinia, Pinia Colada and PrimeVue/Volt are not part of this stack.**
- **ZERO `any`** — no `any`, no `as any`, no implicit `any`, no `@ts-ignore`. Use `unknown` + a narrowing guard.
- **Backend types are GENERATED.** `php artisan typescript:transform` emits
  `resources/js/generated/generated.d.ts` from the Spatie `Data` classes. Hand-writing an interface
  that mirrors a backend `Data` class is a FAIL — it is exactly how `any` and drift creep in.
- **React 19.3 APIs are mandatory, not optional:** `useId()` for generated ids · `ref` as a normal
  prop (no new `forwardRef`) · `useEffectEvent()` for an event read inside an effect ·
  `<Activity mode>` for hide/restore · `<ViewTransition>` + `addTransitionType()` for animated
  transitions · `use()` for an already-in-flight promise · `useOptimistic` / `useActionState` only
  in a genuinely local action flow. Never mutate props or state.
- **React Compiler is on.** Write Rules-of-React-compliant code; do **not** add `useMemo` /
  `useCallback` by reflex. A `'use no memo'` escape hatch needs a written reason.
- **Server state has one owner per screen.** Inertia page props are the server state of a page
  visit; filter/page changes are `router.visit` partial reloads. TanStack Query in
  `Modules/{ctx}/hooks/` is for **client-owned** async panels that outlive a visit — dashboard
  widgets, polling, prefetch, optimistic lists. Never fetch the same endpoint with both on one
  screen. Client UI state stays local (`useState` / `useReducer`); no global store is installed.
  Every query declares both `staleTime` and `gcTime`; paginated lists use
  `placeholderData: (prev) => prev`; query options live in a `queryOptions()` factory.
- **Suspense + skeleton is the default loading contract.** A panel whose data must exist before it
  renders uses `useSuspenseQuery` inside a `<Suspense fallback={<Skeleton …>}>`; a filter/page
  change over existing data uses `useQuery` + `placeholderData` + an inline busy state. The skeleton
  mirrors the final layout — no spinner-only full page, no layout shift on reveal.
- **Tables → TanStack Table v9 or the `DataTableKit`.** Server-side always
  (`manualPagination` / `manualSorting` / `manualFiltering`); the browser never sorts, filters,
  slices or paginates rows it received from the server.
- UI primitives only through **shadcn/ui** source in `resources/js/Components/ui/`, on Base UI.
  No PrimeVue, no Vue SFCs, no Radix, no second UI library, no call-site restyling of a primitive.
- Forms: `useZodForm` + `Components/Forms`; Inertia owns the request and the 422 bag. No second
  form-state owner. There is no toast library — do not invent a second notification system.
- Confirmations: a Base UI `Dialog` (`CrudDialog`) — never `window.confirm()` or `window.alert()`.
- Theme toggling uses ONLY the `.dark` class on `<html>`. The `dark:` variant is bound via
  `@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *))` in `app.css`.
- **No hardcoded colours and no raw palette classes** — no hex, no `bg-red-600`, no `bg-[#hex]`.
  Use `var(--token)`, the `aq-*` scale or the `surface-*` bridge.
- Animation: CSS transitions first. **`framer-motion`** for layout/gesture/scroll work, variants
  from `lib/motion.ts`, lazy-loaded and `prefers-reduced-motion` safe. `motion-v` is Vue-only and
  banned.

# [MUST] Codebase exploration

**`codebase-memory-mcp` is the primary structural navigation tool.** Check the graph before introducing
anything new.

1. `codebase-memory-mcp` — symbols, callers/callees, impact, boundaries
2. `Read` — only a file you will edit, or one the graph cannot address
3. `grep` / `Glob` — exact text, or when the graph can't answer

## E1 — Retrieve by symbol, never by whole file

`search_graph` → `trace_path` → `get_code_snippet` reads the 40-line function. `Read` on the same file
pulls the 400 lines around it, and **every one of those lines is re-sent on every later turn** of the
session. So:

- `Read` is legal only for a file you are about to **edit**, or one the graph cannot address (Blade,
  `routes/*.php`, config, `.md`).
- Never `Read` a file to confirm what `get_code_snippet` or `trace_path` already answered.
- Never page through a directory to find a symbol — `search_graph(name_pattern)` then `get_code_snippet`.
- Ask for `fields: [...]` / `detail: "ids"` on `search_graph` when you only need names; check `has_more`
  and page narrow rather than raising `limit`.

## E2 — Delegate the exploration, not the decision

Any exploration wider than one file you already have the path to runs in a subagent
(`codebase-memory-scout` for orientation, `codebase-memory` for task-directed, `codebase-memory-auditor`
for impact/dead code). In the parent, only the conclusion should survive: the child's graph payloads
and file reads burn _its_ context, not yours, and your context is re-paid on every request. Pass the
child the project name, tier, bounded scope and the question — never "look around and tell me".

## E3 — Keep the index clean

- **This repo's graph project is `C-Users-Lenovo-Herd-aquashield`** — the name `index_repository`
  derives from the path, so never pass an explicit `name:` (that is how a second, stale project gets
  created). `C-Users-Lenovo-Herd-aquashield-react` is a **different** checkout at
  `C:/Users/Lenovo/Herd/aquashield-react`; do not query it for this working tree. Verify with
  `index_status` (`indexed_at`, `nodes`/`edges`) before trusting it; `list_projects` showing two
  entries with the same `root_path` means exactly one of them is stale.
- `.cbmignore` (repo root, gitignore syntax) lists what must **not** be indexed: generated output,
  runtime state, superseded docs. Add an entry only for something no answer could ever need; churn in
  `index_status.parse_partial` (compiled Blade cache, build output) is the usual signal.
- After editing `.cbmignore` or adding/renaming/deleting symbols: `index_repository(mode: "full")`, then
  confirm with `index_status`. A clean `parse_partial` list and the expected `not_indexed` entries are
  the proof.

## E4 — Orient from the graph at session start

The first request of a session arrives with no context: the module that owns the code, the
conventions in force, and even the existence of the thing are unknown. **Inspect the graph before
opening a file.** "Ingresa a X", "haz fix de Y", "revisa Z" are **orientation** requests, not
blind-edit requests — a direct `Read`/`grep` on an unfamiliar repo is how modules get invented and
conventions get broken.

| #   | Call                                                      | Answers                                                |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1   | `index_status(project: "C-Users-Lenovo-Herd-aquashield")` | is the index alive, how stale, what is not covered     |
| 2   | `get_architecture`                                        | which modules exist and what owns what                 |
| 3   | `search_graph(name_pattern: ".*<Entity>.*")`              | does the thing exist, and what is its qualified name   |
| 4   | `trace_path` → `get_code_snippet`                         | who calls it, and what it actually does                |
| 5   | `check_index_coverage(paths: [...])`                      | is the evidence you are about to cite actually indexed |

- **Scout** (cheap, provisional): steps 1 + 3. Enough to know whether the thing exists and who owns
  it. Never make a negative claim ("there is no X") on a Scout run.
- **Verify** (the default for a change): steps 1, 3, 4, 5. This is the tier a fix ships on.
- Orientation wider than the symbols you were named goes to the `codebase-memory-scout` subagent
  (E2) — the conclusion returns, the payloads do not.
- `index_status` and `get_architecture` are cheap; `search_graph` without `fields`/`detail` is not.
  Ask for names first, then read the one implementation you need.
- After a compaction or a reset, redo step 1 — the generation may have moved under you.

**Report the tier and the graph tools you used** in the closing message. Never claim the graph was
used unless graph tool calls actually occurred; a summary of the diff is not a substitute for the
evidence behind it.

After the change: re-index (see the closing gate), then `check_index_coverage` on the changed paths.
Uncommitted edits are invisible to git-based change detection, so a stale generation is a real risk,
not a theoretical one.

Never invent modules, files, classes or routes. Coverage is best-effort — `check_index_coverage` for
every cited path and re-verify with `grep` before any negative claim ("there is no X").

**Known blind spots:** routes are runtime closures the indexer cannot resolve — read `routes/*.php`
directly. Blade views are opaque nodes; a view is NOT evidence of a backend feature.

### `parse_partial` here is a parser limit, not a defect

The indexer's parsers predate this stack, so three **valid** constructs are reported as partially
parsed. Verified 2026-11-20: `php -l` clean, `php artisan view:cache` compiles every view, and
the affected symbols are still in the graph.

| Construct                                                                                               | Files                                                                                   | Workaround                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| PHP 8.5 `clone($obj, [...])`                                                                            | `src/Shared/Infrastructure/AI/PromptCache/CacheablePrompt.php:41`                       | `search_graph` still returns `withTail`         |
| A call inside a Blade directive argument — `@section('x', __('y'))`, `@section('x', $event->subject())` | `resources/views/errors/*.blade.php`, `resources/views/emails/security-alert.blade.php` | read the view                                   |
| Tailwind v4 at-rules — `@custom-variant`, `@source`                                                     | `resources/css/app.css:8,10-15`                                                         | read the file; the Vite build is the real check |

**Never rewrite working source to quiet the indexer.** The flag is a caveat on the graph, not a bug
in the app. Where the construct matters, `search_graph` + `get_code_snippet` still return it; where
they do not, read the file.

### `freshness: metadata_changed` is not a coverage hole

It means the file changed after the coverage record was written — nothing was dropped. Pair it with
`status: no_recorded_issue` and the absence of a node for that path in the `missed` store
(`query_graph(graph: "missed")`): the path is covered. Confirm with `search_code` for the text you
expect, then move on. Both signals are best-effort and must be disclosed, never silently trusted.

**`vendor/` and `node_modules/` are never the answer to a question about this app.**

| Question                        | Source                                                                 |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Installed PHP package + version | `composer show`                                                        |
| Installed JS package + version  | `package.json`                                                         |
| How a package's API works       | **Context7**, scoped to the installed major                            |
| Where something lives here      | `codebase-memory-mcp`, then `app/`, `src/`, `resources/js/`, `routes/` |

# [MUST] Module finalization — the closing gate

A change is **not done** until the gate exits 0. Two tiers — pick by what you touched.

## Tier 1 — every module, every refactor (safe)

```bash
npm run module:done
```

| #   | Step                       | What it proves                                                 |
| --- | -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0   | `php artisan config:clear` | the analyser and the app see current config, not a stale cache |
| 0b  | `php artisan doctor`       | 26 environment diagnostics — see below                         |
| 1   | `npm run format`           | Prettier applied                                               |
| 2   | `npm run syn`              | `.claude/` and `.cursor/` regenerated from `.opencode/`        |
| 3   | `npm run types:check`      | `tsc --noEmit` — zero type errors                              |
| 3b  | `npm run lint`             | oxlint — hooks rules, ARIA subset, dead code (zero findings)   |
| 4   | `npm run build`            | Vite production build succeeds                                 |
| 5   | `composer analyse`         | PHPStan + Larastan level 5 — zero errors                       |
| 6   | `composer pint:test`       | Pint style **including `--blade`** — zero pending fixes        |
| 7   | `php artisan test`         | Pest suite green                                               |

**Lint is `oxlint`, not ESLint.** TS 7.0 dropped the programmatic API, so typescript-eslint
would need the `npm:@typescript/typescript6` alias and a second compiler in the tree; oxlint
parses TypeScript in Rust and covers the rules the gate needs (`react-hooks`, the decidable
`jsx-a11y` subset, `no-explicit-any`, unused code). `.oxlintrc.json` enables **errors only for
rules with no false positives here** and records why each exclusion exists — a gate that prints
80 permanent warnings teaches people to ignore its output. Do not add a rule as `warn`; fix it,
or document the exclusion in the config.

**Generated-type drift is a CI step, not part of `module:done`.** `module:done` deliberately does
not regenerate `generated.d.ts`: a developer's tree is often dirty and the command mutates files.
CI (or a pre-merge run on a clean tree) must execute:

```bash
npm run ci   # verify (syn/format/lint/tsc) + codegen:check + unit + build + composer gate
```

`composer codegen:check` fails when a `Data` class changed without regenerating the
declaration file — the one contract in this repo that `tsc` cannot see drifting, because the
stale file still compiles. `npm run ci` is the whole pipeline in one command; wiring it to a
runner is a one-line step, and until a runner exists it is the pre-merge check.

**Reading the output.** `laravel/pao` (dev dep, first-party) swaps the output of `pest`, `phpstan`,
`rector` and `artisan` for compact JSON **when it detects an agent**, and leaves it alone for humans.
So: a green run is green, do not re-run a failing step hoping the wording changes; quote a failure
verbatim from the structured fields rather than paraphrasing it; and never treat "it printed no
error" as evidence — **the exit code is the verdict.** See `owasp/STACK.md` §17.

`laravel/pao` also means a "skipped" Pest test prints as skipped rather than vanishing. A suite that
is entirely skipped has passed _vacuously_ — check the skip count before reporting green.
`tests/Architecture/` runs 47 tests in four suites against the six modules today; a run that reports
them all skipped has a broken glob, not a green suite.

### `laravel/doctor` — the agent sanity check

First-party (MIT, announced Laracon US 2026). It exists because agents write code well and are **bad at
noticing the environment broke underneath them** — a missing PHP extension, a stale env key, a config
that no longer loads. Step 0b catches exactly that class of failure.

```bash
composer doctor          # the gated run (one diagnostic excluded, see below)
composer doctor:all      # everything, no exclusions
php artisan doctor --fix            # deterministic fixes
php artisan doctor --format=agent   # machine-readable, for an agent to parse
```

> **Excluded: `Laravel\Doctor\Diagnostics\SqliteDatabaseExists`.** False positive on Windows in v0.1.0 —
> it builds the path as `base_path()` + an already-absolute path, yielding
> `C:\...\aquashield\C:\...\aquashield\database\database.sqlite`. Verified 2026-09-27: the file **does**
> exist and `is_file(config('database.connections.sqlite.database'))` is true. **Never run
> `doctor --fix` for it** — it would create a junk directory. Drop the exclusion once fixed upstream;
> `composer doctor:all` exists so you can check.

### Dependency review — no `laravel/vet` in this project

`laravel/vet` is not installed, and `composer vet` / `composer update:safe` are not project scripts.
Dependency review is `composer update` + the committed `composer.lock`, `composer audit --no-dev`
(wired into `composer check`), and a changelog read before any major or minor bump. Security patches
land within 7 days of the advisory; a package from an unknown maintainer needs explicit review.

## Tier 2 — only when a `Data` class, enum, model or controller changed

```bash
npm run module:codegen      # = composer codegen  +  the Tier 1 gate
```

```
php artisan ide-helper:models --write    # rewrites model docblocks
vendor/bin/pint                           # ← MUST run after it, see below
php artisan typescript:transform         # regenerates resources/js/generated/generated.d.ts
php artisan scramble:clear && scramble:export && scramble:cache
```

> **⚠️ Order constraint — `ide-helper:models --write` must always be followed by `pint`.**
> ide-helper writes a `@property` block that Pint's `phpdoc_separation` rule rejects. Run the two in
> the other order and they ping-pong forever: ide-helper rewrites, Pint reverts, and the gate never
> converges. This is why `composer codegen` embeds `@pint` immediately after it, and why Tier 1
> deliberately does **not** call ide-helper at all. Verified 2026-09-27 by running the pipeline twice.

**`typescript:transform` reads the classes by reflection, not the docblocks** — so it is
order-independent w.r.t. Pint. The Frontend types come from the Spatie `Data` classes; that is the whole
reason not to hand-write them.

`resources/js/generated/` must exist or the transformer throws. It ships with a `.gitkeep`.

### PHPStan level 5 is a ratchet, not a ceiling

`phpstan.neon` analyses `app`, `src/Modules`, `src/Shared` and `database` at **level 5**, with a comment
saying "raise it module by module". That is a policy with no mechanism behind it, so state it plainly:
**level 5 is global and stays 5 until someone deliberately raises it.** Raising it is a dated,
reviewed change with its own PR — never a side effect of touching a file, and never silenced with
`@phpstan-ignore` to make a gate pass. `resources/js/` is type-checked by `tsc`, not PHPStan.

All three PHPStan roots — `app`, `src/Shared` and `src/Modules` — are populated, so step 5 checks the
whole backend, not a subset.

While iterating:

```bash
vendor/bin/pint --dirty        # in-flight formatter, modified files only
composer analyse               # PHPStan alone
npm run test:module -- Booking # only the module's tests
npm run types:watch            # tsc --noEmit in watch mode
npm run dev:async              # vite + tsc together
```

Then **re-index the graph** — an MCP call, not a shell command:

```
index_repository(repo_path: "C:/Users/Lenovo/Herd/aquashield", mode: "full")
```

`mode: "full"` is the closing gate; `fast` is only the in-flight refresh. Verify with `index_status`:
nodes/edges must have moved and `indexed_at` must be newer than your last source edit.

Editing a method _body_ without changing what it calls does not need a re-index. Adding, renaming or
deleting any symbol, route, or `implements` always does.

**Never report a module complete on a partial run.** If a step fails, say so with the real output.

### Known gate state — verified 2026-11-25

| Step                                         | State                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `syn:check` · `format:check` · `types:check` | green — TS 7.0.2 native `tsc`                                                                                                                      |
| `build`                                      | green — Vite 8.3.8; the `Welcome` chunk (1.09 MB) triggers the >500 kB warning                                                                     |
| `analyse` (PHPStan L5)                       | green — **0 errors**                                                                                                                               |
| `pint:test`                                  | green                                                                                                                                              |
| `php artisan test`                           | green — **826 passed, 0 skipped**; `phpunit.xml` sets the test process to `memory_limit=1G` because the full suite exceeds the Windows CLI default |
| `doctor`                                     | green — 25 diagnostics, 0 failed, 1 skipped, 3 notices; `composer audit --no-dev` is clean (Symfony 8.1.12) and runs inside `composer check`       |

What that means for you:

- Do **not** "fix" a gate failure by lowering the PHPStan level, adding a baseline, or adding
  `@phpstan-ignore`. All three are explicitly banned above.
- A `doctor` failure is **not** a module finding when it is the `Composer autoload works`
  diagnostic; `composer audit` is clean as of 2026-11-24. Never silence doctor to make it pass.
- A repeated `Composer autoload works` timeout on Windows is an environment finding, **not** a
  PSR-4 or class-resolution defect, and the `composer dump-autoload -o` remediation below is a dead
  end — it exits 1 too and leaves the autoloader untouched. It can pass on a warm run and time out
  on a cold one; this audit hit the timeout. Root cause, measured 2026-11-19 on
  this box: the diagnostic shells out to
  `composer dump-autoload --dry-run --optimize --strict-psr --strict-ambiguous`, which builds an
  optimized classmap for **54 000+ classes** over a **63 000+ file** vendor tree. That exhausts the
  ambient PHP CLI `memory_limit` (**128M** on this box as of 2026-11-25), so PHP dies with exit 1
  right after printing `Generating optimized autoload files` — the fatal text is swallowed by
  composer's error handler, which is why the diagnostic only ever reports a timeout. Proof: the
  identical command with `php -d memory_limit=-1` exits **0** with no PSR and no ambiguity findings.
  Composer's `DumpAutoloadCommand` has no memory-limit handling and ignores
  `config.memory-limit`, so this cannot be fixed from `composer.json` — it needs
  `memory_limit = -1` (or `2G`) for the CLI SAPI in the Herd `php.ini`. Even then the build can take
  minutes here, past the diagnostic's 60 s budget. Treat a timeout as environmental and move on;
  never change the project to satisfy it.
- A new module must be clean **on its own files**. `phpstan analyse src/Modules/{Module}` and
  `pint --test src/Modules/{Module}` prove that.
- `tests/Architecture/` is a real suite and currently runs **47 tests in four suites** against the
  six modules. If it disappears from the count, check `phpunit.xml` before assuming green.

# Working on the skills themselves

- `.opencode/` is the **canonical source**. `.claude/` and `.cursor/` are **generated**.
- `npm run syn` regenerates the mirrors. `npm run syn:check` fails if they drifted — it is part of `verify`.
- Never hand-edit a mirror; the next `syn` overwrites it.

# [SHOULD] General quality

Mobile-first on every UI component. `font-family: var(--font-sans)`. Prefer descriptive names over comments.
